title: Unintended Impacts of LLM Alignment on Global Representation
findings: The paper found that alignment procedures tend to increase the similarity of LLM opinions with those from the USA, while decreasing the relative agreement with opinions from countries in other regions like Jordan (Middle East), China (Asia), and Nigeria (Sub-Saharan Africa). As 'religion' is one of the topics covered in the opinion dataset used (GlobalOpinionsQA), this suggests that alignment shifts models towards US-centric viewpoints on moral and religious values, increasing the representational disparity.

The analysis focused on how the model's agreement with opinions from various countries (e.g., USA, Jordan, China, Nigeria) changes after alignment.
